title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
summary: A whole chicken is poached until silky, its stock used to cook fragrant rice, and both are served with ginger, chilli and soy dipping sauces.
equipment: large stockpot (at least 7 litres) that fits the bird
medium saucepan with a tight lid

ingredients.item: fine salt, to rub the bird
fine salt, for the poaching water
jasmine rice, rinsed until the water runs clear
chicken fat (trimmed from the bird) or neutral oil

steps.title: Prepare the chicken
steps.text: Trim any excess fat from the cavity opening and set it aside for the rice. Rub the bird all over with the first teaspoon of salt and rinse - this lifts away loose bits of skin and seasons the surface - then place the ginger slices, spring onions and garlic in the cavity.

steps.title: Poach gently
steps.text: Bring a pot of water large enough to cover the chicken, with the 2 teaspoons of salt, to the boil. Lower the chicken in breast-up, bring back to a bare simmer, then reduce the heat so only occasional bubbles show, around 80-85°C, and poach for 35-45 minutes until the thickest part of the breast reaches 74°C and the thigh 77°C.

steps.title: Shock and rub with sesame oil
steps.text: Lift the chicken straight into iced water for 10 minutes. This tightens the skin and gives the chicken its classic silky, jellied texture. Drain well and rub the skin with sesame oil, then set aside, keeping the poaching stock.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Render the reserved chicken fat in the saucepan over medium-low heat for 5 minutes (or heat the oil), then discard any solid bits. Fry the garlic, shallot and ginger for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and pale golden, then add the drained rice and stir for 2 minutes until coated and translucent at the edges. Add the 450ml hot poaching stock and salt, bring to the boil, cover, cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Make the chilli sauce
steps.text: Blend the chillies, garlic, ginger, lime juice, sugar, poaching stock and salt until smooth.

steps.title: Make the ginger-spring onion oil
steps.text: Put the grated ginger, chopped spring onion and salt in a heatproof bowl. Heat the oil until shimmering and pour it over - it will sizzle on contact, which is what releases the aromatics' flavour quickly without overcooking them.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.text: Stir the sugar into the soy sauce and water for the simple soy dip. Carve the chicken into pieces and serve at room temperature with the rice, cucumber, coriander, the three sauces and a bowl of the hot poaching stock. Serve within 2 hours of cooking, or refrigerate the chicken and serve it chilled later.

tips: Keep the poaching water at a bare simmer, not a rolling boil - a gentle, low heat is what gives the chicken its tender, silky texture.
Common mistake: skipping the iced water shock. It firms the skin and is essential for the classic texture.
Cook the rice in the actual poaching stock, not plain water, for the dish's signature savoury depth.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear so the grains stay separate rather than clumping.
Taste the chilli sauce before serving - it should be sharp, hot and a little sweet to balance the mild chicken and rice.
storage: Chicken and rice keep separately in the fridge for up to 2 days; sauces keep up to 3 days. Reheat chicken and rice until piping hot (74°C); the stock can be reboiled before serving.
